speechtext:
Section agreed to.
Section 9 agreed to.
On section 10-Governor in council may create corporations.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
Section 10 has a number of subclauses, one of which is the specific clause which provides for the setting up of these corporations which are to be subsidiary to Trans-Canada Air Lines. In connection with these subsidiary corporations there is a question I should like to address to the minister. If I recall correctly, when he first introduced this matter he said it was felt that, owing to the different kinds of operations- as, for example, over the Atlantic or over the Pacific, or certain new services across Canada -it was desirable to have separate corporations. He said that the experiences in flying these different routes would be different. Is it envisaged to have some sort of coordination of these various companies, so that they will learn from each other's experience; in other words, is there to be a coordination of all the lines under the T.C.A., instead of leaving' too much to the subsidiaries by themselves?
Trans-Canada Air Lines

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
The lines will be coordinated through common ownership by T.C.A. Training facilities for all lines will probably rest in T.C.A., as they do to-day. The operations of the system will be directed by officials of T.C.A. The purpose of the subsidiary companies is more for accounting than anything .else: it is to make sure that the accounts of the various operations are kept separate.
Mr. HAZEN': When this section came be-:ore the committee on railways and shipping ;he Minister of Munitions and Supply said that it was to provide for the formation of subsidiary companies to operate certain ocean routes. His words are found on page 281 of the evidence. That was the purpose of this section; I should like to lay emphasis on the words "to operate certain ocean routes." If that is the purpose of section 20, why does it not say so in section 20? Why has that section been made so broad? If the intention was as I have stated, the draftsmanship is very bad, because the intention is not limited by the draftsmanship to the purpose' which the Minister of Munitions and Supply had in view'. The minister told us that the purpose of setting up these corporations, of which there may be one, or a number, was to establish separate companies to operate ocean routes, not Trans-Canada routes or any lines which fly from Canada to the United States, . but routes to Great Britain or across the Pacific. If that is the purpose, why are those words not contained in the bill? I say that ' the draftsmanship is bad and, if the purpose is as ^tated by the minister, further words should be added to this section. I will therefore move that after the word "corporate" in line 6 there be added the words, "for the organization, operation and maintenance of ocean routes". If those words are added to the section I think it will make the matter clearer and will carry out the intention of the Minister of Munitions and Supply, who is acting as Minister of Transport in connection with this bill.

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: Does the hon. member suggest that there is anything in the present paragraph that defeats the objective announced by the Minister of Munitions and Supply?

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: No; but does it meet the obj ective?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: I think so, yes.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
It is bad draftsmanship in that it gives the minister powers for which he is not asking. He says that it is his intention to establish' one or more corporations to carry

on ocean routes, to establish a line between here and the United Kingdom, to establish another on the Pacific and1 perhaps a third to the West Indies and South America. If that is the objective, why not draft the section so as to cover that and no more? Looking into the future, the minister may find that this section as it is worded may not work to the advantage of the Minister of Transport who will .be carrying out this measure. The minister has told us what he wants. Why not put it in the bill?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: I believe the present drafting covers the situation adequately. We have a bill that meets the purposes intended. The purpose of the bill is to put Trans-Canada Air Lines in a position to enter into transocean aviation and to be equipped to fake such action as may be necessary. It may be necessary to incorporate a company in Brazil; we cannot say. It might very well be necessary under the laws of that country, and I do not see why we should pass an amendment that would make that impossible if it. were needed.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: There is another reason why the section might be amended, and that is that it must be read in conjunction with section 3, which provides that the corporation has the right to purchase and hold1 shares in other companies. Provision is made for the disposition of shares in any company incorporated under section 20, and the companies the minister wishes to incorporate under section. 20 are these ocean routes. .Is the section reads, you can incorporate a company for operations solely in Canada, and then you have the power to acquire their shares. I do not think that is the intention.

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
This paragraph may be
required for the corporate purposes of the company. It is not government policy to do what my hon. friend suggests could be done; but if he is attempting to defeat something which could be done, and which wre have no intention of doing, he might defeat a desirable object having to do with the expansion of Trans-Canada services across the ocean. I see no purpose in following the suggestion of my hon. friend, because I cannot visualize difficulties that might arise from such action.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: Could Trans-Canada Air Lines own shares in competing lines such as Pan-American? It is written loosely enough so that they might be able to do so.

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: It owns a share in Laguardia airport. If it did not it could not fly there.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
May I ask the minister a question, and as usual I am being helpful? Section 23 says that the head

Trans-Canada Air Lines
office of the corporation shall be at such city as the directors may select. Does he not think he has confined himself a good deal? We might like to have it at the Seigniory club. That is a pleasant place, but it is not a city. Everybody is cutting down the minister's authority and I am enlarging it. '

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
There is another reason why the suggestion I have made might be considered, and that is the question of taxation. You might get a company established in some cities where you might have to pay taxes, whereas you would not in others.
Amendment negatived on division.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: Before the section carries, we have before us another bill entitled "An Act to incorporate International Air Transport Association". I should like the minister to explain whether there is any connection between that bill and the air bills that are being presented to the house. Mr. Symington is one of the incorporators of the International Air Transport Association. There may be no connection at all. Will the minister explain that?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: The International Air Transport Association is made up of international air line operators from all parts of the world operating internationally. The headquarters of the association happens to be in Canada and Mr. Symington happens to be president of the organization. Trans-Canada Air Lines is a member of the organization, as is practically every great air line in the world. The headquarters of air transport association being in Canada, it is the desire of the association to incorporate themselves in Canada, and the bill has no connection with this one except that Trans-Canada Air Lines is a member of the association.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
Has that association
power to fix rates?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Section agreed to.
On section 11-Repeal of section 17 by proclamation.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: Does this apply merely To rates on postage and mail?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT

approval of the air transport board. For mail, it is a matter of bargain between the post office and Trans-Canada Air Lines, approved by the governor in council.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: What about freight?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: Trans-Canada Air Lines must file its rate on freight with the air transport board, and the rate filed will then be approved or disallowed.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: The board of railway commissioners wall have nothing to do with the rates?

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext: No.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT
speechtext:
Subsection 5 of section 17 reads:
In fixing the rates as hereinbefore provided, it shall be assumed that the corporation's gross revenue and operating expenses for the current year will be the same as in the preceding year, except in so far as the gross revenue will be increased or decreased by any change in rates.

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT

maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT

speakerposition: Minister of Reconstruction; Minister of Munitions and Supply
maintopic: TRANS-CANADA AIR LINES INCREASE OF CAPITAL-CREATION OF CORPORATION TO OPERATE SERVICES UNDER CONTRACT

Trans-Canada Air Lines
